vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: kubernetes
Version: 1.0.0

The skill bundle is designed for comprehensive Kubernetes and OpenShift cluster management, including operations, troubleshooting, manifest generation, and security audits. All scripts (`argocd-app-sync.sh`, `cluster-health-check.sh`, `generate-manifest.sh`, `node-maintenance.sh`, `pre-upgrade-check.sh`, `security-audit.sh`) use standard CLI tools (`kubectl`, `oc`, `argocd`, `velero`, `trivy`, `az`, `aws`, `gcloud`) to perform actions directly aligned with the stated purpose. There is no evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, persistence mechanisms, obfuscation, or prompt injection attempts in `SKILL.md` to manipulate the agent into unauthorized actions. The security audit and health check scripts are positive indicators of responsible cluster management.

llm.summary: The skill's description matches the included scripts and commands, but the SKILL.md and registry metadata omit required CLIs/credentials and the instructions perform cluster-changing operations (upgrades, drains, syncs, backups) that need privileged access — the mismatch and potential for destructive actions warrant caution.

dimensions.detail: The skill claims comprehensive Kubernetes/OpenShift management and includes scripts that use kubectl, oc, argocd, velero, jq, cloud CLIs (aws/az/gcloud), stern, etc. That toolset is consistent with the stated purpose, but the registry metadata declares no required binaries or credentials — an omission. The skill legitimately needs those CLIs and cluster/cloud credentials to function; the metadata should declare them.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and bundled scripts instruct running commands that modify cluster state (cordon/drain nodes, cluster upgrades, argocd sync with --prune/--force, velero install, backups/restores). These operations require cluster-admin and cloud provider privileges and can be destructive if misused. The instructions assume privileged context without limiting or warning about scope or required safeguards.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec — instruction-only with bundled shell scripts. This is lower risk from an installation perspective because nothing is downloaded at runtime by the skill itself. However, the included scripts will run tools already on the host when invoked.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not declare any required environment variables, but the commands reference many placeholders and implicitly require sensitive credentials/contexts (KUBECONFIG or in-cluster kube credentials, cloud provider credentials for az/aws/gcloud, Velero credentials, ArgoCD credentials). Asking for or running under such credentials without declaring them is disproportionate and increases risk of accidental privilege escalation or data exposure.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and no install changes to other skills or global agent settings. The skill does not request persistent presence or modify other skills' configs.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to implement real Kubernetes/OpenShift operations and includes useful scripts, but it assumes you will run it with cluster-admin and cloud provider credentials. Before installing or invoking it: (1) Review the scripts line-by-line and test them in a safe environment (non-production cluster or sandbox). (2) Ensure required CLIs (kubectl, oc, argocd, velero, jq, stern, az/aws/gcloud) are installed and that you understand which credentials the commands will use (KUBECONFIG, environment AWS/AZURE/GCP vars). (3) Do not provide persistent or elevated credentials to an automated agent; prefer manual execution or read-only/dry-run modes first. (4) Be careful with operations that can delete resources (argocd --prune, kubectl drain, velero restore) and with generated Secret manifests — replace placeholder secrets and avoid committing real secrets into Git. If you want higher assurance, ask the skill author to update metadata to declare required binaries/credentials and add safety checks (dry-run flags, confirmation prompts, limited-scope operations).
llm.findings:
[uses-kubectl-oc-argocd-velero] expected: Scripts call kubectl, oc, argocd, velero and other cluster tools — expected for a cluster management skill, but these commands require elevated privileges.
[uses-cloud-clis-aws-az-gcloud] expected: SKILL.md shows commands for AKS/EKS/GKE (az/aws/gcloud) which legitimately require cloud provider credentials; the skill metadata does not declare these needs.
[uses-jq-stern] expected: Utilities like jq and stern are used for parsing and multi-pod logging; expected but undeclared as required binaries.
